rhythm.monday: each lane picks one class or item from the board; owners post the plan line on their card
rhythm.tuesday_wednesday: sweep, rule, fork CI run; second passes on Wednesday
rhythm.thursday: one batch to the maintainer (PRs with run links); an evidence note on #464 only when a complete item exists; one operator line (batch coordinator)
rhythm.friday: board updated; baselines rechecked; I-RC verify lines in (batch coordinator, runners)
rhythm.first_batch: Thursdays; phase 2a first (K10, K04, K15, the CI branch, the K01 worklist); dates on the board, set by lane owners once lanes are claimed

phases.2a: first value: K10, K04, K15, CI branch, K01 worklist

rhythm.between_batches: no single-site PRs unless a gate is red
rhythm.board: GitHub Project on a contributor fork (fallback: one pinned issue there); board link added when it exists; columns class -> lane -> owner -> rule -> sweep PR -> fork run -> second pass -> batch -> gate; not chat: chat is for questions, the board is the state; this folder carries the definitions
rhythm.registry: doc/bug-classes.md shipped in the first class PR: id, name, pattern, rule, status (swept / rule only / not counted / evidence), lane, sites open at the last sweep and the head counted on, example PRs; until it lands upstream the public mirror is ../05-bug-classes.md

flow: class check against doc/bug-classes.md (add a class if new)
if the class touches validation, fork choice, attestation or the MatMul frontier -> E-CONSENSUS evidence; stop here
count sites on the live head (under 3 real sites: file the rule alone)
sweep every site + write the rule (test, lint or CI job)
PR with the fork CI link: fails before, passes after
second pass by the lane's reviewer (Wednesday)
merged -> board card moved -> baseline shrinks
rules: Load: one person owns at most 3 lanes and second-passes at most 3; a first-time owner owns 1; lanes that get no work until claimed are stated, not hidden
Second pass is never the owner; a run lane's second pass is an independent run on different hardware
Registry rule: a new report names its class; swept -> gate failure fixed in the rule; not swept -> the class's sweep PR, never an instance fix
Sweep rule (a): a 'not counted' class is counted on the live head first; under 3 real sites, the rule alone
Sweep rule (b): a sweep PR changes nothing beyond its class; anything else it finds goes to the lane worklist or its own PR
Sweep rule (c): no sweep touches validation.cpp, pow.cpp, src/consensus/, script/interpreter.cpp, fork choice or src/matmul/; hits go to E-CONSENSUS
Hot files (net_processing.cpp, modelnet/helper.cpp, node/matmul_trusted_attestations.*): no per-event PR without a model-based test or a split proposal first

Escalation: gate red -> the lane stops new work and fixes the gate; a PR closed without being taken -> never re-filed, becomes evidence or is dropped; owner/second-pass disagreement -> the batch coordinator decides what goes into the batch, question into the Thursday batch; security-relevant finding -> GitHub private vulnerability reporting upstream, never a public issue or chat post; runner cannot reproduce -> the PR waits and the owner investigates

Maintainer interface: one Thursday message per batch; each PR states class, rule, sites, run link and the invariant it keeps; tested fixes only; no stubs, fail-closed workarounds or disabled tests; nothing into #464's frozen set; CI stays on the fork and is offered upstream only on request; 'would the maintainer reject this?' defaults to yes until the PR says why not

AI never: posts, comments, pushes or opens a PR on its own; opens a PR into release-0.34.16 touching the rule (c) set; files a single-site fix for a registered class; puts a fix in a commit linked from a comment; claims a test ran without run link, SHA and platform; adds a stub, fail-closed workaround, skipped test or widened timeout; touches out-of-scope code (sweep rule b); re-runs a baseline tool already run; holds keys, wallets, cookies or tokens on a test box; quotes private chats, names people other than by handle, or states a figure without its source

Programme done when gates G2 (machines on), G3 (about 13 parser targets; 1 exists) and G4 (K10, K04, K15, K01, K05, K08/K16/K17, K06, K19 each with its rule) are true; then the batch shrinks to the weekly ratchet
